name: Abijam
overview: Abijam was a male king from the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Rehoboam. He held the unique role of King of Judah, as noted in 1 Kings 14:31, and is also referred to as Abijah in 2 Chronicles 12:16. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Abijam means '[my] father is Yam [the sea],' while the variant Abijah means '[my] father is y-h-v-h.' These names reflect different theological emphases, with Abijah highlighting a connection to the name of God. Both names are proper names not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Abijam was the son of Rehoboam, explicitly stated in Scripture. It is inferred that Maacah was his mother, and Asa was his son, establishing a direct royal lineage within the tribe of Judah. These relationships frame his place within the Davidic dynasty.
scriptureSignificance: Abijam's significance lies in his role as a king of Judah, continuing the Davidic line through his father Rehoboam and passing the throne to his son Asa. His dual naming as Abijam and Abijah reflects the biblical tradition of variant names for the same individual. His reign represents a link in the unfolding history of God's covenant people in Judah.
